name: TX-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+11 El Paso district with incumbent Veronica Escobar running for re-election
Challenger Adam Bauman raised about $3,300 against Escobar's $1.07 million
Prediction markets price a Democratic hold at roughly 97 percent
No general-election polls or expert ratings; outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Escobar holds a heavily Democratic El Paso seat, is an established incumbent, and out-raised her opponent roughly 300-to-1, while markets price her near-certain reelection; every piece of available evidence points to a safe Democratic hold.
model.watch: With no polling in the race, the outlook could shift only on an unforeseen development such as a major scandal or a drastic national environment change.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Veronica Escobar seeks another term representing this El Paso-based district, which leans about eleven points toward Democrats in its partisan fundamentals. She is a well-established incumbent in a seat Democrats have held comfortably, and no expert ratings flag the race as competitive. Prediction markets price her reelection at roughly 97 percent.

The Republican challenger, Adam Bauman, has raised about three thousand dollars, a negligible sum against Escobar's roughly one million, leaving him without the resources to run a visible campaign. No public general-election polling exists, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan makeup, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap. All available evidence points the same direction: a safe Democratic hold, with the main question being the size of Escobar's November margin.
